nodes.summary: A group $G$ has exactly one irreducible complex representation of each dimension when for every $n \ge 1$ there is an irreducible homomorphism $G \to \mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{C})$ and any two irreducible homomorphisms $G \to \mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{C})$ are equivalent. Representations are arbitrary homomorphisms of the abstract group $G$; no continuity is required.
nodes.title: Groups with exactly one irreducible representation of each dimension

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group. Two homomorphisms $\rho, \sigma \colon G \to \mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{C})$ are equivalent when there is a matrix $P \in \mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{C})$ with $\sigma(g) = P \rho(g) P^{-1}$ for all $g \in G$.
nodes.title: Equivalent representations into $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{C})$

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group and $\rho \colon G \to \mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{C})$ a homomorphism. Then $\rho$ is irreducible when $n \ge 1$ and the only subspaces $W$ of $\mathbb{C}^n$ with $\rho(g)v \in W$ for all $g \in G$ and $v \in W$ are $0$ and $\mathbb{C}^n$.
nodes.title: Irreducible representations into $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{C})$

nodes.summary: It is not the case that a group has exactly one irreducible complex representation of each dimension $n \ge 1$, up to equivalence, if and only if it is isomorphic to $\mathrm{SU}_2(\mathbb{C})$. Here a representation of dimension $n$ is any homomorphism to $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{C})$ of abstract groups, with no continuity required.
nodes.title: McKay's question 16.58 has a negative answer

nodes.summary: A group $G$ has exactly one irreducible complex representation of each dimension $n = 1, 2, \dots$, up to equivalence, if and only if $G$ is isomorphic to $\mathrm{SU}_2(\mathbb{C})$. Here a representation of dimension $n$ is any homomorphism $G \to \mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{C})$ of abstract groups, with no continuity required.
nodes.title: McKay's question on $\mathrm{SU}_2(\mathbb{C})$ (Kourovka 16.58)
